knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}+4\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}x+4\int 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{-3/2}\text{d}x+4\int {x}^{0}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3/2+1}}{(-\frac{3}{2}+1)}+4\left(\frac{{x}^{0+1}}{0+1}\right)+C \\  & =-2\cdot {x}^{-1/2}+4x+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}+4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
